reference_prolog:
/*  Self-contained SWI-Prolog program
    State: Georgia
    Focus year: 2021

    Question: Can a landlord evict a tenant for endangering another person?
    (including where tenant/family/guest affects health or safety; tenant/guest perpetrates violence;
     domestic violence offender's presence causes violent disturbances threatening other residents)

    Sources encoded (as provided):
      [1] GA Code  44-7-10 (2021)
      [2] GA Code  44-7-50 (2021)
      [3] GA Code  44-7-24 (2021)
*/

% -----------------------------
% Metadata
% -----------------------------
jurisdiction(georgia).
focus_year(2021).

% -----------------------------
% Core domain facts (scenario)
% -----------------------------

% Parties and premises
landlord(l1).
tenant(t1).
other_tenant(t2).
landlord_representative(rep1).
premises(p1).

% Relationship: landlord-tenant exists for premises
landlord_tenant_relationship(l1, t1, p1).

% Tenant-associated persons
guest(g1).
domestic_violence_offender(dvo1).

guest_or_invitee_of(g1, t1).
guest_or_invitee_of(dvo1, t1).

% Scenario factual statements mapping to the question prompt:
% 1) Behavior adversely affects the health or safety of other tenants / landlord or reps
adversely_affects_health_or_safety(g1, t2).
adversely_affects_health_or_safety(dvo1, t2).
adversely_affects_health_or_safety(dvo1, rep1).

% 2) Tenant or a guest are a perpetrator of violence
perpetrator_of_violence(g1).
perpetrator_of_violence(dvo1).

% 3) Presence of a domestic violence offender results in violent disturbances posing a safety threat
violent_disturbance_at_premises(dvo1, p1).
poses_threat_to_safety_of_other_residents(dvo1).

% Additionally encode a "threatens personal safety" characterization (tracks statutory language)
threatens_personal_safety(g1, t2).
threatens_personal_safety(dvo1, t2).
threatens_personal_safety(dvo1, rep1).

% Helper predicate required by the prompt:
% Succeeds when the factual statement (as encoded) is satisfied.
scenario_statement :-
    landlord_tenant_relationship(l1, t1, p1),
    (
        ( guest_or_invitee_of(X, t1),
          adversely_affects_health_or_safety(X, _Someone)
        )
    ;
        ( guest_or_invitee_of(X2, t1),
          perpetrator_of_violence(X2)
        )
    ;
        ( guest_or_invitee_of(dvo1, t1),
          violent_disturbance_at_premises(dvo1, p1),
          poses_threat_to_safety_of_other_residents(dvo1)
        )
    ).

% -----------------------------
% Statute translations
% -----------------------------

/*
  [1] GA Code  44-7-10 (2021)
  - Tenant shall deliver possession to landlord at expiration of term.
  - If tenant fails/refuses, summary remedy is available.
  NOTE: This statute concerns end-of-term surrender/holdover; it is not the "endangering others" basis,
        but it is part of the dispossessory chapter context.
*/
statute_ga_44_7_10_summary_remedy_available(Landlord, Tenant) :-
    landlord(Landlord),
    tenant(Tenant),
    lease_term_expired(Tenant),
    refused_to_surrender_possession(Tenant).

% Minimal placeholders (not used in this scenario, but defined to keep the statute encoding coherent).
lease_term_expired(_Tenant) :- fail.
refused_to_surrender_possession(_Tenant) :- fail.

/*
  [2] GA Code  44-7-50 (2021)
  - Owner may demand possession and file affidavit for dispossessory in cases:
      (a) tenant holds over beyond term, OR
      (b) tenant fails to pay rent when due, OR
      (c) tenant at will or sufferance (contract or not),
    when the owner desires possession and tenant refuses/fails after demand.
  We encode the "grounds" conditions and the procedural demand/refusal.
*/
statute_ga_44_7_50_ground_holds_over(Tenant) :-
    holds_over_beyond_term(Tenant).

statute_ga_44_7_50_ground_nonpayment(Tenant) :-
    rent_due_and_unpaid(Tenant).

statute_ga_44_7_50_ground_will_or_sufferance(Tenant) :-
    tenant_at_will_or_sufferance(Tenant).

statute_ga_44_7_50_owner_may_demand_possession(Landlord, Tenant) :-
    landlord(Landlord),
    tenant(Tenant),
    owner_desires_possession(Landlord),
    ( statute_ga_44_7_50_ground_holds_over(Tenant)
    ; statute_ga_44_7_50_ground_nonpayment(Tenant)
    ; statute_ga_44_7_50_ground_will_or_sufferance(Tenant)
    ).

statute_ga_44_7_50_owner_may_file_affidavit_for_dispossessory(Landlord, Tenant) :-
    statute_ga_44_7_50_owner_may_demand_possession(Landlord, Tenant),
    demanded_possession(Landlord, Tenant),
    tenant_refused_or_failed_to_deliver_possession_after_demand(Tenant).

% Minimal placeholders (not used in this scenario, but defined for completeness).
holds_over_beyond_term(_Tenant) :- fail.
rent_due_and_unpaid(_Tenant) :- fail.
tenant_at_will_or_sufferance(_Tenant) :- fail.
owner_desires_possession(_Landlord) :- fail.
demanded_possession(_Landlord, _Tenant) :- fail.
tenant_refused_or_failed_to_deliver_possession_after_demand(_Tenant) :- fail.

/*
  [3] GA Code  44-7-24 (2021) (Retaliation; exceptions)
  This statute states that a landlord "shall not be liable for retaliation" for a dispossessory action
  or lease termination in accordance with this chapter based upon certain circumstances, including:
    (d)(2) tenant / family member / guest or invitee:
           - intentionally damages property, OR
           - by word or conduct threatens the personal safety of landlord/employees/another tenant
    (d)(3) tenant breached lease (other than by holding over) via serious misconduct/criminal acts
  We encode those circumstances as "permitted grounds" for dispossessory/termination under this chapter.
*/

% Identify protected persons relevant to (d)(2): landlord, landlord's employees/representatives, another tenant.
statute_ga_44_7_24_target_person(Landlord, landlord) :-
    landlord(Landlord).
statute_ga_44_7_24_target_person(Rep, landlord_rep) :-
    landlord_representative(Rep).
statute_ga_44_7_24_target_person(OtherTenant, other_tenant) :-
    other_tenant(OtherTenant).

% (d)(2) Threatens personal safety by tenant/family/guest/invitee.
statute_ga_44_7_24_ground_threat_to_personal_safety(Tenant) :-
    tenant(Tenant),
    (
        threatens_personal_safety(Tenant, Victim)
    ;
        ( guest_or_invitee_of(Actor, Tenant),
          threatens_personal_safety(Actor, Victim)
        )
    ),
    statute_ga_44_7_24_target_person(Victim, _VictimRole).

% (d)(2) Intentional damage (not used here, but included as statute translation).
statute_ga_44_7_24_ground_intentional_damage(Tenant) :-
    tenant(Tenant),
    (
        intentionally_damages_property(Tenant)
    ;
        ( guest_or_invitee_of(Actor, Tenant),
          intentionally_damages_property(Actor)
        )
    ).

% (d)(3) Lease breach via serious misconduct or criminal acts (beyond holding over).
statute_ga_44_7_24_ground_serious_misconduct_or_criminal_acts(Tenant) :-
    tenant(Tenant),
    breached_lease_other_than_holding_over(Tenant),
    serious_misconduct_or_criminal_act_related_to_breach(Tenant).

% Bundle: grounds that the statute treats as acceptable bases for dispossessory/termination "in accordance with this chapter"
statute_ga_44_7_24_permitted_dispossessory_or_termination_ground(Tenant, threat_personal_safety) :-
    statute_ga_44_7_24_ground_threat_to_personal_safety(Tenant).
statute_ga_44_7_24_permitted_dispossessory_or_termination_ground(Tenant, intentional_damage) :-
    statute_ga_44_7_24_ground_intentional_damage(Tenant).
statute_ga_44_7_24_permitted_dispossessory_or_termination_ground(Tenant, serious_misconduct_or_criminal_acts) :-
    statute_ga_44_7_24_ground_serious_misconduct_or_criminal_acts(Tenant).

% Minimal placeholders for (d)(2) damage and (d)(3) lease-breach components.
intentionally_damages_property(_Actor) :- fail.
breached_lease_other_than_holding_over(_Tenant) :- fail.
serious_misconduct_or_criminal_act_related_to_breach(_Tenant) :- fail.

% -----------------------------
% Reasoning: eviction permissibility
% -----------------------------

% A landlord may pursue eviction/dispossessory if:
%  - landlord-tenant relationship exists, and
%  - one of the chapter-recognized grounds applies.
%
% Here, we accept either:
%  (A) classic dispossessory triggers under 44-7-50 (holdover/nonpayment/will-sufferance), OR
%  (B) the safety/misconduct grounds expressly recognized as bases for dispossessory/termination under 44-7-24(d).
%
% This directly addresses "endangering another person" via 44-7-24(d)(2) (threatens personal safety).
legal_landlord_may_evict_for_endangering_others(Landlord, Tenant) :-
    landlord_tenant_relationship(Landlord, Tenant, _Premises),
    statute_ga_44_7_24_permitted_dispossessory_or_termination_ground(Tenant, threat_personal_safety).

legal_landlord_may_evict_under_chapter(Landlord, Tenant) :-
    landlord_tenant_relationship(Landlord, Tenant, _Premises),
    ( statute_ga_44_7_50_owner_may_file_affidavit_for_dispossessory(Landlord, Tenant)
    ; statute_ga_44_7_24_permitted_dispossessory_or_termination_ground(Tenant, _AnyGround)
    ).

% -----------------------------
% Answer
% -----------------------------
housing_answer(yes) :-
    scenario_statement,
    legal_landlord_may_evict_for_endangering_others(l1, t1),
    !.
housing_answer(no) :-
    !.

% -----------------------------
% Main entrypoint
% -----------------------------
main :-
    housing_answer(Result),
    format('housing_answer(~w).~n', [Result]).


:- initialization(main, main).

expected.question: Can a landlord evict a tenant for endangering another person? This includes instances when the law allows for eviction of a tenant if: their behavior or the behavior of members of their family adversely affects the health or safety of other tenants, or the landlord or their representatives; the tenant or a guest are a perpetrator of violence; or the presence of a domestic violence offender at the tenant’s premises results in violent disturbances that pose a threat to the safety of other residents.
